title: Schema-driven caller adapter reference & soft-retry playbook
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an SDK-side reference implementation and playbook for schema-driven function/tool calling adapters across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Goals: deliver a consistent developer ergonomics story, provide safe retry semantics, make streaming function outputs resumable, and ship cross-language examples and tests.

Why now:
- Increasing customer demand for reliable tool-calling patterns (idempotency, retries) and better streaming ergonomics.
- Multiple SDKs have divergent patterns; unify approach to reduce long-term maintenance and improve observability.

Scope:
- Language-specific bindings: TS codegen + runtime helpers, Go codegen + marshaling hooks, Python runtime-first validators with optional codegen.
- Runtime helpers: soft-retry controller, idempotency key helpers, schema validation with coercion rules, streaming checkpoint and resume tokens, telemetry hooks.
- Examples and migration guide for existing integrations.

Non-goals:
- Replacing customer's backend retry/orchestration logic.
- Full-blown formal verification of schemas (we rely on JSON Schema + pragmatic extensions).
acceptance_criteria: Reference adapter implementations exist in SDK repos for Python/TypeScript/Go
Integration tests demonstrating: successful call, safe retry, resume from streaming checkpoint
Benchmarked end-to-end latency overhead <= 2% for common call patterns
API docs + example snippets in sdk-examples repo
Observability: metrics for retry_count, schema_validation_failures, resume_success_rate appear in Console
tasks: Design doc: finalize cross-language schema contract and coercion rules (confluence link below)
TS: implement codegen that outputs typed function stubs + runtime validator wrapper
Go: generate structs and Unmarshal hooks that accept both strict and permissive modes
Python: implement pydantic-based runtime validator + optional decorator for strict type-checking
Runtime: implement SoftRetryController with safe/unsafe function classification and exponential backoff with jitter
Streaming: define resume token format and KV-cache pointer semantics; implement checkpointing API
Examples: add three end-to-end examples (email-sender, db-lookup, multi-step toolchain) in sdk-examples
Telemetry: add metrics & traces, wire to Console dashboards and add alert for high schema failure rate
Docs: migration guide and playbook for choosing retry policy and stream resume settings
comments: 2026-03-01 - Leah Chen: Created ticket after arch sync. Initial draft attached to design_docs. Decided to reuse JSON Schema core but allow 'x-coerce' extension for permissive languages.

2026-03-03 - Marco Reyes: Spike complete for TS codegen prototype; emits typed stubs + runtime wrapper that performs lightweight validation. Prototype PR linked. Observed minimal runtime overhead when validation is shallow.

2026-03-04 - Asha Patel (review): Request: add an explicit idempotency helper that derives keys from function name + stable serialized args and support pluggable store (redis/s3/kvs). Also asked for example of unsafe side-effects and policy to prevent retries.

2026-03-05 - Marco Reyes: Implemented SoftRetryController v0.1. Design: functions mark themselves safe/unsafe; safe functions get retries with backoff (base=100ms, max=5s) and full jitter; unsafe functions fail fast. Added metrics retry_count and retry_errors.

2026-03-06 - Design review: Decision: TypeScript and Go will prefer compile-time generation for most teams, Python will default to runtime validators for ergonomics but provide optional stubs generator for strict deployments.

2026-03-07 - Marco Reyes: Streaming checkpoint format proposed: base64("v1|func:<name>|seq:<token_idx>|kv:<sha256>"). Resume semantics: service can accept resume token and replay missing outputs by referencing KV-cache snapshot. Added spec to design_doc.

2026-03-08 - QA: Found edge case: schema-validation rejects numbers serialized as strings in strict mode. Plan: add configurable coercion rules per-field and language default maps (Python permissive, Go strict, TS strict but opt-in coercion).
2026-03-09 - Security: Reviewed idempotency helper and recommended TTL defaults and HMAC signing for resume tokens. Added requirement to expose ability to rotate signing keys.

2026-03-10 - Marco Reyes: Merged Python runtime helpers PR to main (see PR). TS & Go PRs open for final tweaks. Added examples for email-sender and db-lookup to sdk-examples. Next: finalize docs and add e2e tests for resume flow.
notes:
Implementation decisions & trade-offs:
- Validation format: JSON Schema core + small 'x-coerce' extension. Pros: widely supported; Cons: extension adds interoperability burden.
- Retry semantics: SoftRetryController enforces policy surface that SDKs expose declaratively to app authors. This avoids leaking infra behavior into business logic.
- Streaming resume: resume token ties to service-backed KV snapshot; ensures we avoid replaying side effects. Trade-off: requires service support for snapshotting/garbage collection.
- Developer ergonomics: Python defaults to permissive coercion to match Python duck-typing expectations; TS/Go favor stricter compile-time checks.
